surface_mechanism_description: The HfCl4 molecule interacts with the -OH terminated surface through ligand exchange with either 1 or 2 -OH groups, leading to two different adsorption geometries: apical attachment resulting in the adsorbed species -O-HfCl3 and release of one Cl atom through the formation of one HCl molecule, or edge attachment resulting in the adsorbed species -O-HfCl2 and release of two Cl atoms through the formation of two HCl molecules.
evidence: The HfCl4 molecule may interact with the–OH terminated surface by ligand exchange with either 1, or 2–OH groups, 13 leading to two different adsorption geometries: an apical attachment, resulting in the adsorbed species –O – HfCl3 and the release of one Cl atom through the formation of one HCl molecule; or an edge attachment, resulting in the adsorbed species –O – HfCl2 and the release of two Cl atoms through the formation of two HCl molecules. 14
